# Control your TV and streaming apps with Alexa voice commands

**Hook:**
Imagine lying on the couch and saying, “Alexa, play The Traitors on Netflix,” and the show starts instantly. This beginner-friendly guide shows you how to set up Alexa so you can control your TV, change channels, and launch streaming apps using only your voice.

## Before you start
- An **Amazon account** (free)
- An **Alexa-enabled device** (Echo Dot, Echo Show, or the Alexa app on your phone)
- A **smart TV or streaming device** (Fire TV Stick, Apple TV, Chromecast, or a TV with Alexa built-in)
- Roughly **10 minutes** of your time

> ⚠️ Alexa can’t control every TV or streaming service. Check [Amazon’s list](https://www.amazon.com.au/gp/help/customer/display.html) to confirm your device and service are supported. If yours isn’t listed, you may need a **Fire TV Stick** or similar device.

---

## Step 1 — Link your TV or streaming device to Alexa

**Action:** Connect your TV or streaming device to Alexa so it can understand your voice commands.

**What you see:** Open the **Alexa app** on your phone or tablet. Tap the **Devices** icon (it looks like a house) at the bottom-right corner.

**What happens next:** A list of device types appears. Tap **TV**.

**If it looks different:** Look for a **+** or **Add Device** button in the top-right corner instead.

💬 Example:
Tap **TV** → choose your brand (e.g., Samsung, Sony, Fire TV) → follow the on-screen prompts to sign in with your TV account.

**You’ll know it worked when** your TV or streaming device appears in the **Devices** list in the Alexa app.

---

## Step 2 — Enable voice control for your streaming apps

**Action:** Turn on voice control for apps like Netflix, Stan, or Disney+ so Alexa can launch them for you.

**What you see:** In the Alexa app, go to **Devices** → choose your TV → tap **Enable voice control**.

**What happens next:** A list of supported apps appears. Toggle each app you want Alexa to control (e.g., Netflix, Stan, Prime Video).

**If it looks different:** Some TVs may ask you to open the app on your TV first, then say, “Alexa, discover devices.”

💬 Example:
Toggle **Netflix** and **Stan** to **ON**.

**You’ll know it worked when** the toggles turn blue and the apps appear under **Supported Apps** in the Alexa app.

> ⚠️ Alexa can’t control every app. If your app isn’t listed, you may need to use a **Fire TV Stick** or similar device for full voice control.

---

## Step 3 — Test your first voice command

**Action:** Say a simple command to confirm Alexa understands your TV and apps.

**What you see:** Stand near your Alexa device and say, “Alexa, turn on the TV.”

**What happens next:** Your TV should turn on. If it doesn’t, check that the TV is powered on and connected to the same Wi-Fi as your Alexa device.

**If it looks different:** If your TV doesn’t respond, try saying, “Alexa, turn on [your TV brand]” (e.g., “Alexa, turn on Samsung”).

💬 Example:
“Alexa, turn on the TV.”

**You’ll know it worked when** your TV screen lights up.

---

## Step 4 — Launch a streaming app with your voice

**Action:** Open a streaming app like Netflix using only your voice.

**What you see:** After your TV is on, say, “Alexa, open Netflix.”

**What happens next:** The Netflix app should launch on your TV. If it doesn’t, check that Netflix is installed and enabled in the Alexa app (Step 2).

**If it looks different:** If Netflix doesn’t open, try saying, “Alexa, launch Netflix on [your TV brand].”

💬 Example:
“Alexa, open Stan.”

**You’ll know it worked when** the Netflix or Stan app appears on your TV screen.

---

## Step 5 — Change channels or search for shows

**Action:** Use voice commands to find and play specific shows or movies.

**What you see:** With Netflix open, say, “Alexa, search for The Traitors.”

**What happens next:** Alexa sends the search to Netflix. The results appear on your TV.

**If it looks different:** If the search doesn’t work, try saying, “Alexa, play The Traitors on Netflix.”

💬 Example:
“Alexa, play The Traitors on Netflix.”

**You’ll know it worked when** the show starts playing automatically.

---

## Step 6 — Control playback with your voice

**Action:** Pause, resume, or rewind without touching the remote.

**What you see:** While a show is playing, say, “Alexa, pause,” “Alexa, play,” or “Alexa, rewind 10 seconds.”

**What happens next:** Alexa sends the command to your TV or streaming app. The playback responds immediately.

**If it looks different:** If the command doesn’t work, try saying, “Alexa, pause the TV.”

💬 Example:
“Alexa, rewind 30 seconds.”

**You’ll know it worked when** the show pauses, resumes, or rewinds as you requested.

---

## Common mistakes

- **Mistake:** Alexa doesn’t respond to your voice.
  **Fix:** Check that your Alexa device and TV are on the same Wi-Fi network. Restart both devices if needed.

- **Mistake:** The app doesn’t launch when you say, “Alexa, open Netflix.”
  **Fix:** Confirm Netflix is enabled in the Alexa app (Step 2). If it’s still not working, try restarting your TV or streaming device.

- **Mistake:** Alexa changes the volume instead of pausing the show.
  **Fix:** Say, “Alexa, pause the TV,” or check that your TV’s volume isn’t set to maximum.

---

## What this means for you

- **In everyday life:** No more hunting for the remote. Just say, “Alexa, play The Bachelor on Stan,” and relax while the show starts instantly.

- **For your business or work:** If you use a TV for presentations or video calls, Alexa lets you start a meeting or play a tutorial without touching the remote — great for small offices or home workspaces.

- **If you're just getting started:** Start with turning your TV on and off, then add one streaming app. Once you’re comfortable, try searching for shows or pausing playback.

---

## Try it now

Open the Alexa app on your phone, go to **Devices**, and add your TV. Then say, “Alexa, turn on the TV,” and watch it respond. You’ve just taken the first step toward a remote-free living room!
